deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening of §1, 'Structures modérées sur un espace', of the tame-topology notes. Grothendieck first sets up the purely set-theoretic layer before adding topology on the next page.

(1) Setting. X is a set and F is a family of subsets of X. The three conditions are: stable under finite unions, stable under finite intersections, stable under complement. The margin bracket and arrow show they were relabelled, as the later text confirms: a) = complement, b) = finite unions, b') = finite intersections. Together they say F is a Boolean subalgebra of P(X).

(2) Functions instead of sets. Let A_F ⊂ Z^X be the set of finitely-valued functions f: X → Z whose fibres f^{-1}(n) all lie in F.
- φ_A ∈ A_F exactly when A and X−A lie in F (assuming ∅ ∈ F).
- So condition a) (complement-stability) is equivalent to a'): every characteristic function φ_A with A ∈ F lies in A_F.
- F is recovered from A_F as {A : φ_A ∈ A_F}. So giving F is the same as giving the subset A_F ⊂ Z^X.

(3) Ring structure. Given a), the following are equivalent: b) (unions), b') (intersections, by De Morgan), and b''): A_F is stable under finite products. Note φ_A·φ_B = φ_{A∩B}, and products of step functions have fibres that are finite unions of intersections of fibres. A_F is then also closed under sums and negation, hence is a subring of Z^X; the manuscript slips and writes X^Z.

(4) Arbitrary coefficients. Everything works with Z replaced by any commutative ring Λ. A_F is then a sub-Λ-algebra of Et(X,Λ), the algebra of step functions (finitely many values) X → Λ, and F is determined by it.

(5) Characterising the image (continued on the next page). For Λ a domain with fraction field K, the subalgebras arising this way are exactly the saturated ones: λ ≠ 0 and λφ ∈ A imply φ ∈ A. Equivalently, they are the traces on Et(X,Λ) of sub-K-algebras of Et(X,Λ) ⊗ K ≅ Et(X,K). Over a field K every unital subalgebra of Et(X,K) is spanned by idempotents (a subalgebra of K^n is ≅ K^m), so it corresponds to a Boolean algebra.

Purpose. This algebraizes a 'tame' family of subsets as a ring of constructible (step) functions. The next page imposes topological conditions: F stable under closure and interior, so the frontier and the partition into interior, exterior and frontier stay in F, with local closedness and connected components in F. These are the first axioms of a tame/stratified structure on a space, i.e. the beginning of Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée'.
errors: Slip: 'sous-anneau de X^Z' should read Z^X (or Λ^X).

Labels: the conditions were renumbered in the manuscript (complement = a), unions = b), intersections = b')). Read literally with the original a), b), c) order, the later sentences ('moyennant a) les conditions b) et b') sont équivalentes') make no sense.
Minor gap: A_F is only nonempty and well behaved if ∅ ∈ F (or X ∈ F); this is implicit.
Over a general commutative ring Λ, unital vs non-unital subalgebras matter (the 'unitaire' was struck out). The image characterisation is only stated for domains, which is correct there.

ideas.what: Boolean algebra of subsets encoded as the ring A_F of finitely-valued Z- (or Λ-) valued functions with fibres in F; F ↔ A_F bijective, and finite-intersection stability ↔ multiplicative closure
ideas.modern_name: Stone correspondence between Boolean algebras and Boolean rings / rings of locally constant functions on the Stone space; ring of constructible functions
ideas.where_published: Constructible functions with Z coefficients appear around SGA 4/SGA 5 and the Deligne–Grothendieck conjecture on Chern classes of constructible functions; not this exact formulation

ideas.what: For Λ a domain with fraction field K, the subalgebras of Et(X,Λ) of the form A_F are exactly the saturated ones (traces of sub-K-algebras of Et(X,K))
ideas.modern_name: Saturated / pure subalgebras; subalgebras of K^n are split, i.e. generated by idempotents

ideas.what: Using a ring of Z-valued constructible functions as the primary datum of a 'tame structure' on a space (to be refined by topological closure conditions on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Algebra of constructible functions in o-minimal / subanalytic geometry (Euler calculus)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schapira, Viro (~1988–91); o-minimal setting van den Dries
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses tame topology but, as far as I know, not this function-algebra formulation

missed.claim: Grothendieck's tame-topology axiomatics starts from the ring of Z-valued constructible (step) functions attached to the Boolean algebra of 'tame' sets, rather than from the sets themselves. This anticipates the later habit of treating constructible functions and Euler integration as the natural algebraic invariant of o-minimal or subanalytic structures. Only mildly new: the algebra itself is classical Stone duality.
missed.quote: et par suite la donnée de F équivaut à celle de la partie A_F ⊂ Z^X ... A_F est une sous-Λ-algèbre de Λ^X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that the function-ring viewpoint, the one linking to Euler calculus and motivic or Grothendieck-ring-of-definable-sets ideas, was present at the very foundation of Grothendieck's tame topology, earlier than Esquisse (1984).

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is classical Stone-type duality and routine verification. Its interest is purely historical: it is the opening of Grothendieck's own axiomatics of 'structures modérées', framed through rings of constructible functions, plausibly predating the o-minimal literature. The substantive content is elementary.
transcription_corrections: The three initial conditions were relabelled by Grothendieck (bracket and arrow in margin): complement = a), finite unions = b), finite intersections = b'); the transcription keeps the obsolete a), b), c).
'{+moyennant c)+}' under a') should read 'moyennant a)' (or refers to the relabelled condition).
'il l'est de [?] [?] par f ↦ -f' likely reads 'il l'est de même par f ↦ −f'.
'Lorsque Λ est intègre [?] des corps [?]' reads 'Lorsque Λ est intègre de corps des fractions K' (continued on next page).
On the next page, 'EH(X,Λ)' should be 'Et(X,Λ)' (fonctions étagées).
Manuscript has 'X^Z' (author's slip for Z^X); the transcription correctly reproduces it but it should be flagged.
Crossed-out first line is likely 'X ensemble topologique' (struck out because topology is introduced later).
